Tax optimization: all payments under the leasing agreement are attributed to the cost of production, thereby reducing the taxable base for income tax. Savings for the lessee due to no property tax obligations, as the leased asset usually remains on the leasing company's balance sheet. Ability to acquire and use property without diverting the enterprise's own funds all at once. Ability to acquire ownership of the leased asset, completely free from tax burden, upon expiration of the leasing contract. Independent selection of the leasing subject and its seller by the lessee.
credit_page.type1_desc: The lessor (leasing company) acquires ownership of the property specified by the lessee from a certain seller and transfers this property to the lessee as a leasing object under certain conditions for temporary possession and use. The property transfers to the lessee provided that all leasing payments are made.
credit_page.type2_desc: The property is not bought out by the lessee, but remains the property of the leasing company and, after the expiration of the leasing contract, is leased or rented out again.
credit_page.type3_desc: An enterprise buys property with its own funds and then applies to a leasing company. This is one way to quickly return working capital. The leasing company considers the property as a leasing object and purchases it under a sales contract from the enterprise. The same property is then leased back to the same enterprise.
